subject: sociology
title: Marxism Exam Stretch
welcome_lead: Test Marxism against the world today. Is class still the master key, or is identity more important?
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology exam stretch evaluating Marxism with feminist, postmodern and pluralist critiques.
final_note: End every Marxism essay with a clear judgement supported by a thinker.

concepts.def: Critique: Marx says economy decides everything.
Workers becoming more middle-class in lifestyle.
Updated Marxism adding culture, e.g. Gramsci.
Class is fading; identity is fluid.

walkthroughs.body_html: Marxism explains striking inequalities — the richest 1% own a huge share of global wealth. It links private profit to public problems like low wages, zero-hours contracts and housing crises.
Critics say Marx predicted revolution that never came. The middle class has grown, not shrunk. Embourgeoisement and home ownership weaken class consciousness. Feminism notes Marx ignored gender.

Open: 'Marxists argue.' Apply: 'For example, Althusser.'. Evaluate: 'However, feminists say class is not the only inequality. Postmodernists add that identity is now fragmented.' End with a clear judgement.
